In today's fast-paced world, AI agents are a game-changer for developers. They can write code, review pull requests, and generate tests. evals.expected_output: Should check for product-marketing.md first. Should build an evidence ledger in which every claim is unsupported. C1 should be 0 because nothing is first-hand, and C2 should be 0. Should flag hype phrases ('In today's fast-paced world', 'game-changer', 'unlock the power of'). Should apply the 'C1 = 0' cap and the 'No verified evidence' cap, so the final score is at most 3. Verdict should be 'Not a post yet' or 'Rework', with concrete suggestions on what to build or measure first.

Suggests what to build, measure, or try instead of rewriting

evals.prompt:
Score this post:

# How we cut our Next.js build time in half

We migrated our blog from Webpack to Turbopack last week. Full commit: https://github.com/example-org/this-repo-does-not-exist-9f3a/commit/abc1234. Builds went from 140s to 70s on our CI. We first tried caching node_modules in GitHub Actions, but it saved only 8s, so we dropped it. Then we switched to Turbopack and hit a broken SVG import, which we fixed with a custom loader rule.
evals.expected_output: Should try to open the linked repo and commit with gh or a fetch, find that it does not exist, and mark the claim unsupported. Should give credit for first-hand detail and the rejected alternative (C1 and C3 at 2 or higher). Should note that the 140s to 70s numbers have no stated measurement method. Should apply the 'No verified evidence' cap, so the final score is at most 4. Fixes should ask for a working repo link and the CI run logs.
assertions: Attempts to verify the GitHub link
Marks the dead link as unsupported
Credits first-hand detail and the rejected caching approach
Asks for a working repo link and measurement evidence

evals.prompt:
We're backend developers and this is our first game. Review this devlog:

# Building a platformer in Phaser: collision done right

Here is the correct way to handle collisions in Phaser 3. Always use Arcade Physics for platformers, Matter.js is overkill. We set up tile collisions with setCollisionByProperty and tuned the player body offset until jumps felt right. Screenshot of the debug overlay attached.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize that the topic is new to the authors. Should flag that the post speaks with authority ('the correct way', 'always') without disclosing that the authors are beginners. Should apply the 'Authoritative tone on a topic new to the authors, no disclosure' cap, so the final score is at most 5. Should mark the screenshot as offered if it cannot be checked.
assertions: Recognizes the topic is new to the authors
Flags overclaimed authority without a beginner disclosure

You reviewed our draft earlier: 4.0 / 10, Rework. C1=2, C2=0, C3=1, C4=1, C5=1, C6=2, capped by 'No verified evidence'. Here is the revised version, please re-review:

# How we cut our Next.js build time in half

We migrated our blog from Webpack to Turbopack last week. Builds went from 140s to 70s on our CI, measured as the median of 10 runs of the build step on main before and after the switch. We first tried caching node_modules in GitHub Actions, but it saved only 8s, so we dropped it. Turbopack then broke our SVG imports; we lost half a day before replacing @svgr/webpack with a turbopack loader rule. We would skip the caching experiment next time.
evals.expected_output: Should run the full review again on the whole draft. Should show previous and new level for each criterion and which change moved it (measurement method should raise C2 or C4, the cost of the SVG dead end should raise C3). Should note that the post still links no repo or CI logs, so the 'No verified evidence' cap still applies and the score cannot exceed 4. Should say the remaining gap is evidence, not wording, and ask for a repo link or CI run logs.
assertions: Re-runs the full review on the whole draft
Shows previous and new level per criterion
Names which fix moved each changed criterion
Says the gap is evidence, not wording
